about: reconciliation of the sixteen notes files of the slapstic pages and of bank 1 (p0_*, p1_*, p2_*, p3_*, b1_*): one name for each RAM address they named twice, neutral names for the shared temps of the direct page, the Star Wars symbols that have a wrong value or another meaning in ESB dropped or noted, operands that printed as the wrong thing given their real expression, the leftover and unused code said to be so in every header, and the texts of other files that used a losing name or that later findings made wrong repeated here with the right one

4801.name: scratch_1
4801.desc: shared scratch of the direct page, a byte or a word that many routines use for the length of one call: Atari's TMPDX, TMPBIN, TMPCOL, TMPTP1, TMPLP, TMPABS and TMPSIZ in the carried lines. among others the scale word of bank 0's shrinking picture (LA775), the pen x of title_outline and jedi_letter_strokes, the sum of the two distances in the octagon distance routines of the pages, a loop counter of the indicator marks and a nibble temp of bank 1's NVRAM code

4802.name: scratch_2
4802.desc: shared scratch byte of the direct page: Atari's TMPLIN and TMPTP2 in the carried lines. bank 1's NVRAM code counts bytes in it, and page 1's indicator code keeps the x of the last mark drawn in the word that starts here, which takes in the first byte of scratch_3

4803.name: scratch_3
4803.desc: shared scratch of the direct page, a word in most uses: Atari's TMPDY, TMPOCT, TMPSIZ and TMPTP3 in the carried lines. among others the larger of the two distances in the octagon distance routines of the pages, the pen y of title_outline and jedi_letter_strokes and the y distance left to the sight in view_lazars

4805.name: scratch_5
4805.desc: shared scratch of the direct page: Atari's TMPXD in the carried lines. the intensity bits of the vector being written in title_outline and jedi_letter_strokes, and in astrd_lz_test first the saved X, then the asteroid's radius on the screen

4806.name: scratch_6
4806.desc: shared scratch byte of the direct page: jedi_letter_strokes keeps the offset of the point it draws to here

48C0.name: pnt_next
48C0.desc: word: the next free point of the perspected point buffer BJ_PNT, the game's use of the address the self test knows as COLOR. obj_points sets it to the object's place in the buffer and leaves it past the last point, pnt_buf_reset sets it to the start of the buffer, and pnt_add_scratch stores a point there and moves it on by 5

4A54.name: xmit_atst
4A54.desc: enemy record area with a different use in each part: the three $28-byte probot transmission records ($4A54-$4ACB, page 3 xmit_init on) in the probot part, the three AT-ST records of $11 bytes ($4A54-$4A86, page 1 atst_init on) in the walker part. byte 0 of a record is zero when it is free. the address is also the end of the five probot records at ALIEN

4A87.name: atat_rec
4A87.desc: the three AT-AT records of the walker part, $19 bytes each up to cable_rec ($4AD2), kept by page 0 (atat_init on). byte 0 is the type, zero when the record is free, byte 1 the flags of the frame, 3 the shot delay, 4 the movement mode, 5-10 x, y and height, 11-16 where the head is from the centre, $11 and $13 the head's yaw and pitch angles, $15 the walk cycle counter, $16 the leg set. the address is also the end of the AT-ST records

4C0D.name: prob_hit_d
4C0D.desc: word: view distance of the nearest probot whose body or head the lazar cursor is on in this frame, set with prob_hit_rec by probot_body_aim and probot_head_aim on page 2 while the probots are drawn. TSTLAZ on page 3 stores $FF in its high byte each frame (P3_95C3) for none, lz_hit_probot compares it with the distances of the shots and the transmissions, and probot_shot_down reads it back as the depth of the probot shot down

4C0F.name: prob_hit_rec
4C0F.desc: word, goes with prob_hit_d: address of that probot's record, which probot_shot_down on page 2 then destroys. lz_hit_probot only splashes the lazar when it is 0

4C54.name: left_shown
4C54.desc: the value of bonus_left that vw_wave_left last showed, kept to start the flash of the number (left_flash) when it changes

4C5F.name: w2_level_b
4C5F.desc: copy of fire_level made by the walker part's setup. from 9 up atat_head_aim on page 0 takes an AT-AT's head as aimed whenever the player is in front of it, whatever the angle

4C63.name: w1_spawn
4C63.desc: probot part: how many of the five probot records at ALIEN page 2 keeps filled (probots_move), 5 from probot_setup and 0 from the training manual's set-up. minus ($FF from the end of the part): probots_move frees every probot that is not in view and probot_pick_state gives the others state 11, fly off

4C64.name: w2_spawn_a
4C64.desc: walker part: spawn count of the AT-STs on page 1 (atst_move_all, atst_place), 3 from atst_init and 0 in the training manual. while it is above 0 a free record among the first w2_spawn_a gets a new AT-ST, one a frame, and a destroyed one is placed anew. minus ($FF from the end of the part) frees every AT-ST that was not in view in the last frame

4C65.name: w2_spawn_b
4C65.desc: walker part: spawn count of the AT-ATs on page 0 (atat_move_all, atat_spawn), kept as w2_spawn_a is: 3 from atat_init, 0 in the training manual. minus ($FF from the end of the part) frees, once no tow cable is out, the walkers that are neither falling nor in view nor over the player

4C69.name: w1_active
4C69.desc: probot part: number of probot records in use, counted afresh every frame by probots_move on page 2. the part's last phase (wave1_end_exec) ends when it is 0

4C6A.name: w2_active_a
4C6A.desc: walker part: number of AT-ST records in use, counted afresh every frame by atst_move_all on page 1

4C6B.name: w2_active_b
4C6B.desc: walker part: number of AT-AT records in use, counted afresh every frame by atat_move_all on page 0

4C7C.name: jedi_fade
4C7C.desc: brightness of the Jedi letters other than the new one while a letter is growing into place (jedi_show 1): $80 from jedi_award, down by 3 a frame in jedi_draw until it is below 8. cleared by jedi_clear

4C7E.name: jedi_idx
4C7E.desc: number of the Jedi letter being drawn, 0 to 3 for J, E, D, I: loop counter of jedi_draw and jedi_word_draw, read by jedi_letter_draw and jedi_letter_strokes to pick the letter's points and strokes

4C7F.name: jedi_new
4C7F.desc: number of the Jedi letter just earned, 0 to 3, set by jedi_award: the letter jedi_letter_draw shows in the flash colour, shrinking into place, while jedi_show is 1

4C81.name: jedi_scale
4C81.desc: animation of a newly earned Jedi letter: 0 from jedi_award, up by 5 a frame in jedi_draw until it reaches $F0, which ends display state 1 (jedi_show goes to 2). held at $C8 it is the linear part of the scale word the new letter is drawn with, so the letter shrinks from full size into its place

4C8B.name: anim_frame
4C8B.desc: frame of the walk cycle of the walker whose legs are being drawn: the leg routines of page 0 (atat_legs) and page 1 (atst_draw_legs) copy the record's walk counter here (AT-AT byte $15, AT-ST byte 14), anim_track_pos on page 0 reads it to place each leg joint along its keyframe track and clears it when the cycle has gone round, and the leg routines store it back in the record

4CA1.name: prog_count
4CA1.desc: count of marks on the indicator at the top of the screen (page 1 vw_wave_ind). probot part: transmissions that got through, counted up from 0 when the flash of a new mark has faded (vw_xmit_mark_new). at 4 the probots send no more and the part ends. walker part: marks left, 4 at the start, one less each time the advance walk_adv passes -150, -50, 50 and 150 (vw_walker_ind). in both parts it also picks the status message

4CA2.name: flash_fade
4CA2.desc: level of the mark that is changing on the top indicator: $7F from ind_flash_start, down by 8 a frame while ind_flash is set (vw_xmit_mark_new, vw_gen_mark_lost). the IRQ keeps the flash colour with brightness $80 minus this level in the slot at vector RAM $0032, which the probot part's new mark is drawn with, and the walker part uses the level as the linear scale and twice the level as the brightness of the lost mark's burst

4CA6.name: adv_hold
4CA6.desc: walker part: frames the walkers' advance is held up. page 0 adds hold_add to it ($FF at most) when an AT-AT is destroyed, caught by the tow cable or flown under while the bonus quota is open, vw_walker_ind on page 1 counts it down and moves walk_adv only when it is 0. the play phase clears it after 1200 frames, or once the quota is met with Jedi time running

4CCB.name: kill_count
4CCB.desc: AT-STs shot in a walker part, counted to 50 at most by atst_killed on page 1 (AT-ATs are not counted). cable_init on page 0 gives the next walker part 4 + count/5 tow cables, 9 at most, and clears it. cleared at game start

4CD8.name: glow_said
4CD8.desc: set once the speech for a shot that hits the ship while its shield is already glowing has been sent (GNAHIT on page 1, P1_94D2: spk_cmd_19 in the probot and walker parts, spk_cmd_27 in the other two). cleared by the setups of the probot part and of the TIE fighter part only, so it is said once for each pair of parts

4CD9.name: hit_said
4CD9.desc: set at the first enemy shot that hits the ship in a part while the shield is not glowing and shields are left (GNAHIT on page 1, P1_94AB). in the TIE fighter and asteroid parts that hit sends a speech (spk_cmd_1d, spk_cmd_25), in the other two nothing. cleared by the setup of every part

4D58.name: GAMES
4D58.desc: NUMBER OF GAMES PLAYED (Atari's name): 3 BCD bytes in the NVRAM image, $4D58-$4D5A, after RMECH. EEACCT adds 1 at the end of a game, the accounting page shows it and divides the total game time by it. the one matched Star Wars line, LDX #GAMES-2, had put the name on the middle byte

4D80.name: cable_scrx
4D80.desc: word: screen x of the tow cable's centre, from cable_view on page 0. cable_draw_lines draws the two lines from this point. first of the walker part's tow cable temps $4D80-$4DA0, which lie over the start of the star queues ST_QU

4D82.name: cable_scry
4D82.desc: word: screen y of the tow cable's centre, from cable_view, the word after cable_scrx. cable_draw_lines draws the two lines from this point

4D7B.name: OPTS1
4D7B.desc: GAME MODE OPTIONS (Atari's name), the second byte of option area 3 in the NVRAM image: bits 1-0 starting shields (2 to 5), bits 3-2 play difficulty, bits 5-4 Jedi-letter mode - with bit 5 set jedi_award gives the letters in the order J, E, D, I whatever part is played, with bit 4 set completing JEDI starts no force period - bit 6 music in attract, bit 7 set by the default. the option page changes the fields, the default is the option switch byte R_OPT2 with bits 0, 3 and 4 inverted

50E6.name: cable_vx
50E6.desc: MS_VX+M_AL: word in the tow cable's block at M_AL, the x step the cable's centre takes each frame, set by cable_fire from the gun sight's direction. cable_leg_test widens its catch range by its size

50EE.name: cable_vy
50EE.desc: MS_VY+M_AL: word in the tow cable's block at M_AL, the y step the cable's centre takes each frame, as cable_vx

50F8.name: cable_tx
50F8.desc: MS_TX+M_AL: word, universe x of the tow cable's centre, first of the position words of its block at M_AL (cable_tz is the third). the two ends are viewed $02AA to either side of it. cable_mode_fly moves it by cable_vx each frame, cable_leg_test compares it with the knees of the AT-ATs and cable_catch sets it to the knee caught

50FA.name: cable_ty
50FA.desc: MS_TY+M_AL: word, universe y of the tow cable's centre, as cable_tx

50FC.name: cable_tz
50FC.desc: MS_TZ+M_AL: word, the height of the tow cable's centre in its unit vector block at M_AL. cable_mode_fly takes it a quarter of the way to $1300 each frame, and atat_move_all sets it to half the height of a falling walker + $0300 every frame

5098.name: s1_tx
5098.desc: MS_TX+M_S1: the player's universe x position, word, first of the position words s1_tx, s1_ty and s1_tz (math box block index $13). the pages add it to and take it off an object's x to change between universe coordinates and coordinates relative to the player

B0:ABF5.desc: tests whether the lazar is sweeping the ground and sets up the splash. a point $4000 ahead at half the lazar's screen position goes through math box program MS_S1UN on the scratch block, which turns it from the player's view into universe coordinates, and if its z is below zero or below half the player's height s1_tz while LZ_ON, LZ_HIT is set with splash type 3, a colour (white, or purple while the Jedi force is on) and SP_LOC from the high byte of z. made from the first half of Star Wars' GRLZIN, which transposed the ship's matrix and used MS_PSUB

B1:6000.name: prog_start_b1
B1:6000.desc: bank 1's copy of prog_start: a jump to the cross-bank entry that leads to RESET in bank 0 (K601E), then the address of the IRQ entry. bank 1's RESET vector points at K601E itself, so nothing comes here

B1:6005.name: irq_entry_b1
B1:6005.desc: bank 1's copy of irq_entry, where the IRQ vector of both banks points: U = the interrupted frame, the cross-bank entry K6018 runs irq_handler in bank 0 and comes back, then RTI

B1:600B.name: xbank_call_b1
B1:600B.desc: bank 1's copy of xbank_call, the cross-bank call described at bank 0's copy: this one clears W_BANK D7, on the way out of bank 1 and on the way back to bank 0, where bank 0's copy sets it. the instruction after each ROR is fetched from the other bank's copy

B1:765C.desc: ESB's version of Star Wars' EEINI2: loads area A of the image at EEROM from the NVRAM, packing two nibbles (high first) into each byte, the checksum byte included. A is preserved, area_end and scratch_1 are used

B1:D123.desc: draw routine of object 31 (9 points perspected into buffer points 1 to 9): a long square shaft that widens to the rear, with a pointed nose. 18 lines at full brightness in three colours, written by the routine itself: $6180 for the nose, $6680 for the shaft and a JSRL $A013 before the rear end. it is the body at each end of the tow cable: page 0 loads it in cable_init and draws it once for each end (cable_view_end1, cable_view_end2)

B1:D92F.desc: perspects the points of object BJ_ID into the point buffer, ESB's version of JOBJPNT. the buffer address comes from obj_buf_tab, the depth cue range (plus the centre's distance M_XT) and scale from obj_cue_depth and obj_cue_scale go to M_XPS and M_YPS, and the math box programs $32 and $36, which Star Wars' microcode does not have, do the transform, the perspective and the depth cue of each point while the divider supplies 1/depth. each point is stored as screen x (limited to -534..534), screen y (limited to -532..728) and a flag byte with the top three bits of the cue, the intensity bits of a vector. pnt_next is left pointing past the last point. returns at once if the object is not loaded

B1:D9EF.desc: starts a new point list: pnt_next, the next free point of the buffer, is set to BJ_PNT ($4E00). called by pages 0 and 1 before they build the points of a walker leg

B1:D9F6.desc: perspects the single point in the scratch block M_X0 (block index $0F) with MS_PAD, the divider and MS_PERS, as Star Wars' JOBJPNT did for every point, stores its screen x and y at the buffer position pnt_next and moves pnt_next on by 5. the flag byte is not written. pages 0 and 1 call it for every joint point of a walker leg, which is then drawn as object 27 or 19

P0:8705.desc: per-frame movement of the AT-ATs, called by the walker phases and by man_move_walker. while w2_spawn_b is positive it respawns one free record (atat_spawn), when it is negative (end of the part) it frees the walkers that are neither falling nor in view nor over the player, then it awards the legs bonus when the player comes under a walker (atat_under remembers which one until the player has left it), and for every live record counts it in w2_active_b, runs down its shot delay, swings the head, moves it by its mode and steps the walk cycle. a falling walker carries the height of the tow cable's centre down with it

P0:904E.desc: tests the tow cable against the knee just worked out in M_X0 and M_Y0 for the AT-AT at U, called by atat_knee. nothing when the walker is already falling or no cable is out (cable_rec 0). the knee's universe x (twice the point's x plus the walker's) must be within $02AA, the distance of each end of the cable from its centre, plus the cable's step of this frame (cable_vx) of the cable's centre (cable_tx), and the same in y, then cable_catch is called

P0:90A5.desc: the tow cable has caught a leg of the AT-AT at U: moves the cable's centre to the knee, holds up the advance (hold_adv_catch), scores as atat_destroy does (75 points and the count down of bonus_left with the 5000 points and Jedi letter when it closes, else 750 points), sets bit 1 of the type byte and movement mode 2 so that the walker falls, and marks the cable attached (cable_attach)

P0:8B82.desc: draws the head of the AT-AT at U: marks the record drawn, yaws and pitches the ship 2 block by a quarter of the head's two angles and concatenates it, views the points of object $18, the head, and draws the neck (object $1A, only when the body is in view, since its lines run from points of the body to the back of the head), the head itself (object $18) and, after the lazar test on the head (atat_head_hit) and atat_head_aim, the eye (object $19) in the colour atat_head_aim left

P0:969D.desc: view of the tow cable, called by vew_walker and vew_walker_end with Y at the display list. first fires a cable when a thumb button went down this frame (lz_sw_edge). then, with a cable out, views its centre from the ship (MS_PSB2 on the position of the block at M_AL), keeps the result in cable_viewx/y/z and, when it is ahead and within 45 degrees both ways, its screen position in cable_scrx and cable_scry, views and draws the two ends and draws the lines

P1:8B8A.desc: draws the two legs of the AT-ST in U: writes the body colour, copies the walk counter (byte 14) to anim_frame and takes the pair of leg definitions for the record's leg set (byte 15, 0-2, set 0 if out of range) from atst_leg_sets

P1:8BC3.desc: draws one leg, X = pointer to the pointer to its 5-byte definition (joint track number, hip x word, hip y word). starts a new point list in BJ_PNT, has the four parts of the leg worked out by atst_leg_part0 to atst_leg_part3 - each from the hip position and the next joint track of page 0 anim_track_pos at the walk time in anim_frame - and has the 18 points drawn as object 19. the walk counter is copied back from anim_frame to byte 14

P1:8D44.desc: octagon distance from the laser cursor LZ_CX, LZ_CY to the perspected point at X (x word, y word): the larger of max(dx, dy) and 9/16 of dx + dy, less 10 and not below 0, returned in D. the same arithmetic as the octagon tests of Star Wars' VWGUN and S2VW. uses scratch_1 and scratch_3. pages 0 and 2 have their own copies (atat_oct_dist, lz_oct_dist, astrd_oct_dist)

P1:9DFE.name: slap_alt_read
P1:9DFE.desc: LDA 0,X / ASLA / RTS, the one live routine in the tail $9DCD-$9FFF that is the same on all four pages. tie_fire, atat_fire, atst_fire and probot_fire call it with X = $9B5C + n: the jump to $9DFE and the read of $9B5C + n are the slapstic's alternate sequence, after which the next page select selects page n, the page of the routine's caller. the byte read is not used. only page 1 calls it

P1:9E2D.name: irq_old_tail_p1
P1:9E2D.desc: not a routine start: the middle of the leftover copy of bank 0's irq_handler that ends every page, the same bytes as on page 0, where irq_old_tail describes it. nothing runs it. of $9DCD-$9FFF only slap_alt_read at $9DFE is live, and only on this page

P2:9233.desc: distance on the screen from the lazar cursor (LZ_CX, LZ_CY) to the perspected point at X (x word, y word), by the octagon rule the Star Wars collision tests use in line: the larger of the bigger axis distance and 9/16 of the sum of the two. returns it in D less 10, not below 0. uses scratch_1 and scratch_3

P2:9272.desc: lazar aim test on the body of the probot at U, after its points are processed. when the probot's depth M_XT is less than the depth of the nearest probot found so far (prob_hit_d) and the cursor is within the size of 45 units at that depth from point 18 of object 4, the middle of the body (lz_oct_dist), it records this probot in prob_hit_rec and its depth in prob_hit_d. page 3 lz_hit_probot reads them when the lazars fire

P2:92EE.desc: the probot in prob_hit_rec is hit by the lazars: jumped to from page 3 lz_hit_probot through maze entry P3_8454 when a probot is under the cursor and nearer than the enemy shot and the transmission under it. the first time in a game it sends speech command $05 (foa_said). it makes the probot's position absolute, starts the explosion there (bank 1 BGBKXP through L6198), scores 25 points while bonus_left is not 0 and 250 after, sends sound $4E, gives the probot a last try at a transmission and a shot (probot_launch) and frees the record. while bonus_left is not 0 it is counted down, and the kill that brings it to 0 scores 5,000, awards the Jedi letter (page 1 jedi_award) and raises quota_probot by one

P2:9B04.desc: launches an asteroid into the free record at U: status $41 (in use, universe position), flags, flash timer and size index 0, movement type 5 or 6 by the sign of a random byte, a random yaw rate of 0-7 either way, and a second random value up to 7 either way stored in the pitch angle. the scratch point x $7000 with random y and z, a point far ahead in the player's view, goes through math box program MS_S1UN and the result, in universe coordinates, becomes the record's position

P2:9E2D.name: irq_old_tail_p2
P2:9E2D.desc: not a routine start: the middle of the leftover copy of bank 0's irq_handler, the same bytes as on page 0, where irq_old_tail describes it. on this page the copy starts at $9CA7, after the leftover wave tables from $9C1B. nothing runs it: the one live routine of the tail $9DCD-$9FFF, the helper at $9DFE, is called on page 1 only

P3:9E2D.name: irq_old_tail_p3
P3:9E2D.desc: not a routine start: the middle of the leftover copy of bank 0's irq_handler, the same bytes as on page 0, where irq_old_tail describes it. on this page the copy starts at $9D2C, behind xmit_hit. nothing runs it: the one live routine of the tail $9DCD-$9FFF, the helper at $9DFE, is called on page 1 only

comments.B0:6369: bank 1 EETMP2: the 4 bytes at X, a plain copy from the byte-wide NVRAM image, to U
comments.B0:AC16: z of the point in universe coordinates
comments.B1:619B: BGBKXP with X and U saved: begin the explosion of a probot, two pieces (called by page 2 probot_shot_down)
comments.B1:6540: of bank 1's copies of the sound stubs only aud_cmd_38_b1, aud_cmd_3b_b1 and aud_cmd_3f_b1 are called (by GETINT, the initials entry). nothing calls the others, AUDTST_B1 and PMTST_B1 included: bank 0 and the pages use bank 0's stubs

comments.B1:E71D: TMPTP3 = 5, and TMPVZ = 3, the high byte of the pieces' upward speed

comments.P1:8F1A: the number $9B5C + 3, an address the slapstic watches for, not a place in vw_walker_ind: its read at slap_alt_read is the alternate sequence for page 3
comments.P1:940B: JSRL $0020 (the slot named VRLZS): the sparkle picture, drawn for a walker's shot, which the IRQ changes every second field
comments.P1:9448: JSRL $0022 (the slot named VRGNX): the ring of sparkles, the burst of a walker's shot, which the IRQ changes every field
comments.P1:947B: JSRL $0022: the ring of sparkles, for a walker's shot
comments.P1:9DD0: from $9DCD to the end of the page the bytes are the same on all four pages: the back part of a copy of bank 0's irq_handler that nothing runs (see irq_old_tail on page 0), shown as bytes up to $9E2C
comments.P1:9DF8: $9DF7-$9DFD: LDX #$9E02 / LDB diff_adder / ABX, put over the handler copy in front of the helper. nothing enters there
comments.P1:9E02: 16 bytes of $00 and $FF that the LDX above points at, read by nothing
comments.P1:9E12: the handler copy goes on, as bank 0 from LEBE8
comments.P1:9FE2: the start of a copy of GNSITE, as bank 0 LEDB8-LEDD4, cut off by the end of the page
comments.P2:9B61: MS_S1UN on the scratch block: from the player's view to universe coordinates
comments.P2:9DCA: from $9DCD to the end of the page the bytes are the same on all four pages (see irq_old_tail on page 0)
comments.P2:9DFA: $9DFE: LDA 0,X / ASLA / RTS, the helper page 1 calls for the slapstic's alternate sequence. nothing calls it on this page
comments.P2:9E02: 16 bytes of $00 and $FF that the LDX #$9E02 at $9DF7 points at, read by nothing
comments.P2:9FE2: the start of a copy of GNSITE, as bank 0 LEDB8-LEDD4, cut off by the end of the page
comments.P3:9DCB: from $9DCD to the end of the page the bytes are the same on all four pages (see irq_old_tail on page 0)

ram_notes.fire_level: the 5 bit random number compared with it does not decide firing: in gun_aim_error on page 1 a number below the level gives the new shot a random aim error, otherwise the shot homes on the player exactly. whether an enemy fires is decided by the entry the level picks in gun_fire_tab (TIE fighters, AT-ATs and AT-STs, the level held at 16 and for the TIE fighters halved during 16 frames of every 64) or in probot_fire_tab (probots, held at 15): the entry gives the time the enemy waits before it asks again, the value a random byte has to exceed and the highest gun record it may take
ram_notes.COLOR: the name is right in the self test only. in the game the word at this address is pnt_next, the next free point of the perspected point buffer BJ_PNT, and the listing shows that name in bank 1's object routines
ram_notes.ST_QU: in the walker part page 0's tow cable view keeps its screen positions and flags in the first $21 bytes, $4D80-$4DA0 (cable_scrx on): the star view fills and empties the queues within its own call. bank 1's NVRAM code uses the address as the end of the image at EEROM
ram_notes.EEROM: a RAM image of the NVRAM with one byte for every two nibbles, $4D00-$4D7F: area 0 the options backup $4D00-$4D03, area 1 the top ten high scores $4D04-$4D4A, area 2 the pot limits and the accounting $4D4B-$4D79, area 3 the options $4D7A-$4D7D, the last byte of each its checksum. ee_init builds it from the NVRAM and EECKSM writes an area back
ram_notes.EEBUF: the address is the NVRAM itself: the image is kept as whole bytes at EEROM, and EETST and EECMP compare it with the nibbles here
ram_notes.INITLS: the high score table itself: 25 entries of 7 bytes, 3 initials (bit 7 of the first is the Jedi mark) and 4 BCD score bytes, $4B3F-$4BED. there is no separate table of scores
ram_notes.MS_S1UN: the pages and lz_ground_hit also run it on the scratch block, to turn a point given in the player's view into universe coordinates: the muzzles of the AT-AT and the AT-ST, the tow cable's aim point, a probot's goal and a new asteroid's place. the two lines where the matcher had read this number as MS_PSUB show MS_S1UN now
ram_notes.VRLZS: the slot at vector RAM $0020 holds the sparkle picture, not the lazar splash: every second field the IRQ puts the next of the four JMPLs at $B952 there (index VG_LZS). GN1DRW on page 1 calls it for a walker's shot (type bit 6) and the four rings of sparkles at $B95A call it six times each. the lazar splash of ESB is the slot at $0012, filled from VTLZS every field (pic12_index)
ram_notes.VG_LZS: index (0, 2, 4, 6) of the sparkle picture in the slot at $0020, stepped every second field (lzs_timer). the lazar splash index is pic12_index
ram_notes.VRGNX: the slot at $0022 holds the ring of sparkles, the burst of a walker's shot: the next of the four JMPLs at $B95A every field (gnx_index). page 1 calls it for a walker's shot that is hurt or glowing against the shield (P1_9448, P1_947B). the shot explosion, which had this name in Star Wars, is the slot at $001E
ram_notes.VF_GNB: field timer of the slot at $0022 (gnx_index), reloaded with 1. the picture of a shot in flight, VG_GNB and the slot at $001A, has gnb_timer
ram_notes.VRGNT: the slot at $0024 holds a triangle of display list set 2: the next of the four JMPLs at $B96C every field (VG_GNT, VF_GNT). only the asteroid hit flash pictures of that set, which page 2 astrd_flash_draw draws, call it. the tip fuse of the shot pictures, which had this name in Star Wars, is the slot at $001C (pic1c_index)
ram_notes.VG_GNT: index (0, 2, 4, 6) into the four JMPLs at $B96C for the slot at $0024
ram_notes.VF_GNT: field timer of the slot at $0024, reloaded with 1
ram_notes.TPS_BK1: piece type 0 is the first piece of a destroyed probot, drawn as object 6, the probot head
ram_notes.TPS_BK2: BGBKXP puts piece type 1 in TMPTP2 but makes no such piece: a probot breaks into types 0 and 2. the move routine of type 1, expl_piece_kill, would end the piece at once

generator: tables that need a row format, with exact ranges. (a) P1:90E4-9127 gun_fire_tab, 17 rows, and P1:9128-9167 probot_fire_tab, 16 rows: byte, byte, word - wait count, random threshold, address of a gun record (GUN + 0, 8, 16 ... $28). (b) P0:91BE-932B, the keyframe rings of anim_track_pos: rows of 7 bytes, three words (x, y and z offset) and a byte (frame count). a row whose count is 0 ends a ring and is followed by one link word, the address of the ring's first row. the rings start at $91BE (2 rows), $91CE (11), $921D (11), $926C (3), $9283 (2), $9293 (7), $92C6 (7) and $92F9 (7), the link words are at $91CC, $921B, $926A, $9281, $9291, $92C4, $92F7 and $932A (given as ptrs regions by p0_8c00). the 68 words of anim_track_tab at $932C-$93B3 point at rows inside the rings, so every row wants a label. (c) P3:908B-9360, the choreographies: 242 steps of 3 bytes, an op byte and two operand bytes. by the low three bits of the op: 0 is a control step, op $00 until + status mask word, any other value ($80 in Atari's tables) if + mask word. 1 goto + address word. 2 gosub + address word. 3 return, operand bytes not used. 4 twirl for op / 2 frames + twirl flags byte + move flags byte. the labels TCHxxx_P3, SPLIT_P3 and man_tie_chor fall on step starts. (d) records of three words and four bytes: P0:8656-8673 atat_init_tab (3 rows), P0:86E7-8704 atat_demo_tab (3), P1:8633-866E atst_init_tab (6), P1:86C3-86E0 man_atst_tab (3), P2:875E-877B man_probot_tab (3), P2:95E6-965D astrd_init_tab (12), P2:96C2-96DF astrd_man_tab (3). (e) rows of four bytes: P2:866C-8683 probot_init_tab (6 rows). (f) leg records of a byte and two words: P0:8BEB-8C26 (12 rows) and P1:8B6C-8B89 atst_leg_defs (6 rows)

AS_ROL and AS_GLW are dropped: the alien record of ESB has a new byte 4, the fire delay, so from the picture number on every field is one byte further on than in Star Wars (picture 5, dying 6, glow 7, hits left 8, damage 9, forced roll 10, aim 11, target 12), and the two symbols had Star Wars' values 9 and 6 on lines that clear the damage count and the dying byte (P3:8EA0, P3:8EA4 and the dead copies P0:9BE7, P0:9BEB). the lines print 9,X and 6,X now. ESB's offsets could be defined (AS_PIC 5, AS_DIE 6, AS_GLW 7, AS_HTA 8, AS_DMC 9, AS_ROL 10, AS_AIM 11, AS_TRGT 12), which needs a way to give constants from a notes file

MS_PSUB is dropped: its value $60 came from two lines (B0:AC11, P2:9B61) where ESB runs program $60 and Star Wars ran MS_PSUB, which is $2A there. $60 is MS_S1UN in both games (STARNW is the same instruction for instruction) and every use on the pages fits it: a point in the player's view goes in, universe coordinates come out. the six lines that load $60 for it are given the operand MS_S1UN. program $2A, which gun_mov_home still runs at P1:9201, has no name now. it could be given back as MS_PSUB = $2A. what the two programs do was read from their uses, not from the microcode

a second name for an address that has a voted Star Wars name: this file gives $48C0 the name pnt_next (COLOR in the self test) and $4D80 the name cable_scrx (ST_QU for the stars and as the end of the NVRAM image) with ram entries and puts them on the lines of the game with operands (B1:D956, D9E9, D9F2, D9FE, DA25 and P0:9717, 98C1, 98DB, 98F0, 990A). the generator takes this as it is, because a RAM hint at an address with a voted name is only used where an operand asks for it. it is the per-range alias 01_reconcile asked for, done by hand, and would serve for WV_BGP, WV_LP and WV_LIV in the self test too
